title: Watch the patch
steps: Photograph the patch this morning and this evening
Keep it covered and don't share towels
Tell the medical officer if it spreads, blisters or reaches your face
rationale: A burning or tingling patch on one side can be the first sign that the shingles virus is waking up; photos show the medical officer how it changes.

title: Look after your mouth early
steps: Don't share cups, cutlery or towels
Rinse your mouth with water after meals
Photograph the sore for the medical officer
rationale: Mouth or lip sores spread through shared items; early care keeps them small.

title: Rest and drink fluids
steps: Drink water regularly through the day
Skip heavy exercise until you feel better
Check in again this evening
rationale: A sore throat and swollen glands can mean your body is fighting a virus; rest and fluids help.

title: Keep your distance from the crew
steps: Wear a mask in shared modules
Wipe shared handles and controls after use
Eat apart from the crew today
rationale: Fever or a sore throat can mean an infection that passes to your crewmates.

title: Recover after hard work
steps: Stretch gently and drink water
Ask for lighter tasks tomorrow if you are still sore
Check in again tomorrow morning
rationale: Aches and tiredness after a spacewalk or hard work usually settle with rest.

title: Describe it to the medical officer
steps: Tell the crew medical officer what you feel, in your own words
Say when it started and what makes it better or worse
rationale: ORBIT cannot match what you describe to the signals it knows, so a person should look at it.

title: Get medical help now
steps: Stop what you are doing and sit upright
Call the crew medical officer now
Measure your oxygen level with the medical kit
rationale: What you described needs a medical check straight away, whatever your score.
